records.source: בִּשְׁנַת־מוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ עֻזִּיָּ֔הוּ וָאֶרְאֶ֧ה אֶת־אֲדֹנָ֛י יֹשֵׁ֥ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֖א רָ֣ם וְנִשָּׂ֑א וְשׁוּלָ֖יו מְלֵאִ֥ים אֶת־הַהֵיכָֽל׃
records.gloss: In [the] year of [the] death of the king Uzziah, and I saw the Lord sitting on a throne high and lifted up, and his skirts [were] filling the temple.
pieces: In the year King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and towering, and the hem of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} robe filled the temple.

L.1: In the year of the death of King Uzziah, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and the hems of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} [robe were] filling the temple.

R.1: In the year King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord. He was sitting on a throne that was high and raised up. The edges of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} robe filled the whole temple.

decisions.choice: the year King Uzziah died: a date, and the end of a long reign
decisions.reason: Uzziah (also called Azariah) reigned over Judah for fifty-two years (2 Kings 15:1-7; 2 Chronicles 26). He is the first king named in Isaiah's heading (1:1). In the year an earthly king of long standing died, Isaiah sees the true King (verse 5).

decisions.choice: the Lord: the title "Lord, Master", not the divine name
decisions.reason: The word here is the title Adonai. Verse 5 names the one on the throne "the King, Yahweh of hosts". The same title comes again in verses 8 and 11.

decisions.choice: high and lifted up: describing the throne
alternatives: the Lord, high and lifted up, sitting on a throne
decisions.reason: The two words follow "throne" directly and most naturally describe it. They could also describe the Lord himself, as the same pair does in 57:15 (and of the servant in 52:13). Either way the picture is of one exalted far above all.

decisions.choice: his skirts filling the temple: the hem or flowing edges of a royal robe; the temple's main hall
decisions.reason: The word means the lower edges of a garment (Exodus 28:33-34). The temple here is the great hall of the house of God in Jerusalem; the same word also means a king's palace. The vision may reach beyond the earthly building to the heavenly throne room (1 Kings 22:19).

decisions.choice: the hems of his [robe] (Literal); the hem of his robe (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "his skirts", meaning the edges of his robe. "Robe" is supplied so the reader does not picture a modern skirt. Readable says "edges of his robe".

decisions.choice: I saw the Lord. He was sitting on a throne
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long Hebrew sentence into three short ones.

records.heading: The Lord seated on a throne

records.source: שְׂרָפִ֨ים עֹמְדִ֤ים׀מִמַּ֨עַל֙ ל֔וֹ שֵׁ֧שׁ כְּנָפַ֛יִם שֵׁ֥שׁ כְּנָפַ֖יִם לְאֶחָ֑ד בִּשְׁתַּ֣יִם׀יְכַסֶּ֣ה פָנָ֗יו וּבִשְׁתַּ֛יִם יְכַסֶּ֥ה רַגְלָ֖יו וּבִשְׁתַּ֥יִם יְעוֹפֵֽף׃
records.gloss: Seraphim [were] standing above him; six wings, six wings to one; with two he covered his face, and with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew.
pieces: Seraphim stood in attendance over {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and each of them had six wings. With one pair it kept its face covered, with one pair it kept its feet covered, and with one pair it flew.

L.2: Seraphim [were] standing above {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; six wings, six wings [belonged] to each one: with two he covered his face, and with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew.

R.2: Fiery heavenly beings called seraphim were standing above {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Each one had six wings. It used two wings to cover its face and two wings to cover its feet. It used the other two wings to fly.

decisions.choice: seraphim: heavenly beings whose name suggests burning
decisions.reason: The name comes from a word meaning "to burn". Elsewhere it is used of the "fiery serpents" in the wilderness (Numbers 21:6) and the flying serpent of 14:29 and 30:6. Only here are seraphim beings who stand before God's throne. They have faces, feet, hands (verse 6) and voices.

decisions.choice: covering face and feet: reverence and modesty before God
decisions.reason: Even these holy beings do not look on God openly: Moses hid his face before God (Exodus 3:6) and Elijah wrapped his face in his cloak (1 Kings 19:13). Covering the feet probably shows modesty in his presence. The verbs describe what each seraph does continually.

decisions.choice: above him: above the Lord seated on the throne
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers back to the Lord of verse 1. The seraphim stand over him the way servants stand around a seated king.

decisions.choice: it, its (Balanced and Readable); he, his (Literal)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses masculine forms for each seraph, as it does for any noun of that gender. Balanced and Readable say "it" for a heavenly being of unknown form.

decisions.choice: Fiery heavenly beings called seraphim
decisions.reason: Readable explains the unfamiliar name from its meaning (see m1).

records.source: וְקָרָ֨א זֶ֤ה אֶל־זֶה֙ וְאָמַ֔ר קָד֧וֹשׁ׀קָד֛וֹשׁ קָד֖וֹשׁ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת מְלֹ֥א כָל־הָאָ֖רֶץ כְּבוֹדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And called this to this and said, holy, holy, holy [is] Yahweh of hosts; [the] fullness of all the earth [is] his glory.
pieces: And they kept calling to each other, \q "Holy, holy, holy is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies! \q All that fills the earth is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory."

L.3: And this one called to this one and said, \q "Holy, holy, holy [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts; \q the fullness of all the earth [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory."

R.3: They were calling out to each other, \q "Holy, holy, holy is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies! \q His glory fills every part of the earth!"

decisions.choice: holy, holy, holy: utterly holy, holy beyond comparison
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats a word to make it stronger ("temple of the LORD" three times in Jeremiah 7:4; "land, land, land" in Jeremiah 22:29). Saying "holy" three times declares God's holiness in the highest degree. To be holy is to be set apart, wholly other than every created thing and wholly pure. Isaiah's favorite name for God, "the Holy One of Israel", grows from this vision. The living creatures of Revelation 4:8 sing the same threefold word.

decisions.choice: the fullness of all the earth is his glory: all that fills the earth shows his glory
alternatives: his glory fills the whole earth
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the fullness of all the earth [is] his glory". It can mean that everything filling the earth displays his glory, or that his glory is what fills the earth (Numbers 14:21; Psalm 72:19; Habakkuk 2:14). Both say his glory is present everywhere, not only in the temple.

decisions.choice: his glory: the glory John 12:41 says Isaiah saw
decisions.reason: After quoting 6:10, John writes that Isaiah said these things "because he saw his glory", meaning the glory of Jesus (John 12:41).

decisions.choice: this to this: one to another
decisions.reason: The seraphim call back and forth to each other. The verbs show the praise going on and on.

records.source: וַיָּנֻ֨עוּ֙ אַמּ֣וֹת הַסִּפִּ֔ים מִקּ֖וֹל הַקּוֹרֵ֑א וְהַבַּ֖יִת יִמָּלֵ֥א עָשָֽׁן׃
records.gloss: And shook [the] foundations of the thresholds from the voice of the [one who] called, and the house was filled [with] smoke.
pieces: At the sound of the one calling, the bases of the doorways trembled, and smoke filled the temple.

L.4: And the foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of the one who called, and the house was filled [with] smoke.

R.4: At the sound of the voice calling out, the bases of the doorways shook. The temple was filled with smoke.

decisions.choice: the foundations of the thresholds: the supports or sockets of the doorways
decisions.reason: The first word usually means a forearm or a cubit; here it means the bases or pivots on which the thresholds and doors rest. The whole building shakes at the voice.

decisions.choice: the house was filled with smoke: a sign of God's presence
decisions.reason: Smoke and shaking marked God's coming down on Mount Sinai (Exodus 19:18). A cloud filled the temple when it was dedicated (1 Kings 8:10-11), and smoke from God's glory fills the heavenly temple in Revelation 15:8. The smoke may also come from the altar of verse 6.

decisions.choice: the one who called: each seraph as it called
decisions.reason: The word is singular, looking back to "this one called to this one" in verse 3. It means the calling voice of the seraphim.

decisions.choice: the temple
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the house", meaning the house of God named "the temple" in verse 1. Balanced and Readable say "temple" to make clear which house is meant.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֞ר אֽוֹי־לִ֣י כִֽי־נִדְמֵ֗יתִי כִּ֣י אִ֤ישׁ טְמֵֽא־שְׂפָתַ֨יִם֙ אָנֹ֔כִי וּבְתוֹךְ֙ עַם־טְמֵ֣א שְׂפָתַ֔יִם אָנֹכִ֖י יוֹשֵׁ֑ב כִּ֗י אֶת־הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת רָא֥וּ עֵינָֽי׃
records.gloss: And I said, woe to me, for I am destroyed, for a man unclean of lips I [am], and in [the] midst of a people unclean of lips I [am] dwelling; for the King, Yahweh of hosts, have seen my eyes.
pieces: Then I said, "Woe to me! I am finished. My lips are unclean, and the people I live among have unclean lips, and with my own eyes I have looked on the King, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies!"

L.5: And I said, "Woe to me, for I am ruined! For a man unclean of lips [am] I, and in the midst of a people unclean of lips I [am] dwelling; for the King, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, my eyes have seen!"

R.5: I cried out, "How terrible this is for me! I am doomed! I am a man whose lips are unclean. I live among people whose lips are unclean too. And I have seen the King with my own eyes. I have seen {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies!"

decisions.choice: I am ruined: cut off, destroyed
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "be destroyed, cut off" or, from a word that sounds the same, "be silenced". Isaiah fears death, since no one can see God and live (Exodus 33:20; Judges 13:22). "Silenced" would fit his unclean lips, set against the seraphim's praise.

decisions.choice: unclean of lips: unfit to speak in God's presence
decisions.reason: Lips stand for speech. Isaiah has just heard the seraphim praise God, and he knows that his own speech, and his people's, is unclean before the holy King. He does not separate himself from his people: their sin is his. The cure touches his lips (verse 7).

decisions.choice: the King, Yahweh of hosts: God as the true King
decisions.reason: Isaiah dates the vision by the death of King Uzziah (verse 1), and now he names the one on the throne as the King. God as King is a theme of the book (33:22; 41:21; 43:15; 44:6).

decisions.choice: How terrible this is for me!
decisions.reason: Readable puts the cry of distress "woe" into plain words, as it does with the related cry "woe" elsewhere in Isaiah.

records.source: וַיָּ֣עָף אֵלַ֗י אֶחָד֙ מִן־הַשְּׂרָפִ֔ים וּבְיָד֖וֹ רִצְפָּ֑ה בְּמֶ֨לְקַחַ֔יִם לָקַ֖ח מֵעַ֥ל הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
records.gloss: And flew to me one of the seraphim, and in his hand a live coal; with tongs he had taken [it] from on the altar.
pieces: Then one of the seraphim flew to me. In its hand was a glowing coal that it had picked up off the altar with tongs.

L.6: And one of the seraphim flew to me, and in his hand [was] a burning coal; with tongs he had taken [it] from upon the altar.

R.6: Then one of the seraphim flew over to me. It was holding a red-hot coal. It had used tongs to take the coal from the altar.

decisions.choice: a live coal: a glowing coal or a hot stone
decisions.reason: The word means a glowing coal, or perhaps a heated stone (1 Kings 19:6 uses a related word for bread baked on hot stones). Either way it comes straight from the fire of the altar.

decisions.choice: tongs ... the altar: the temple's sacred fire
decisions.reason: Tongs were among the temple utensils (Exodus 25:38; 1 Kings 7:49). The altar may be the altar of incense before the inner room or the altar of burnt offering in the courtyard. On the Day of Atonement the high priest took burning coals from the altar (Leviticus 16:12). Even the seraph does not touch the coal with its hand.

records.source: וַיַּגַּ֣ע עַל־פִּ֔י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֛ה נָגַ֥ע זֶ֖ה עַל־שְׂפָתֶ֑יךָ וְסָ֣ר עֲוֺנֶ֔ךָ וְחַטָּאתְךָ֖ תְּכֻפָּֽר׃
records.gloss: And he made [it] touch my mouth and said, here!, this has touched your lips, and departs your iniquity, and your sin is atoned for.
pieces: It touched my mouth with it and said, "See, this has touched your lips. Your guilt is removed, and atonement is made for your sin."

L.7: And he made [it] touch my mouth and said, "Look, this has touched your lips, and your iniquity departs, and your sin is atoned for."

R.7: It touched my mouth with the coal and said, "Look! This coal has touched your lips. Now your guilt is gone. Your sin is forgiven."

decisions.choice: iniquity ... sin: guilt and wrongdoing
decisions.reason: The first word means wrongdoing and the guilt it brings; the second means missing the mark, failing to do right. Together they cover the uncleanness Isaiah confessed in verse 5.

decisions.choice: is atoned for: covered, wiped away by God's act
decisions.reason: The verb is the word used for the sacrifices of atonement (Leviticus 4:20; 16:30). The passive form shows that it is done for Isaiah, not by him: the cleansing comes from God's altar, and Isaiah only receives it.

decisions.choice: departs ... is atoned for: done now, as the coal touches
decisions.reason: The verb forms follow from "this has touched your lips": as soon as the coal touches him, his guilt goes and his sin is covered.

decisions.choice: Your sin is forgiven
decisions.reason: Readable puts the temple word "atoned for" into plain words. Literal and Balanced keep the language of atonement.

records.source: וָאֶשְׁמַ֞ע אֶת־ק֤וֹל אֲדֹנָי֙ אֹמֵ֔ר אֶת־מִ֥י אֶשְׁלַ֖ח וּמִ֣י יֵֽלֶךְ־לָ֑נוּ וָאֹמַ֖ר הִנְנִ֥י שְׁלָחֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And I heard the voice of [the] Lord saying, whom will I send, and who will go for us? And I said, here I [am]; send me.
pieces: Then I heard the voice of the Lord asking, "Whom am I to send? Who will go on {{deity_pronoun:our|Our}} behalf?" I answered, "I am ready. Send me."

L.8: And I heard the voice of the Lord saying, "Whom will I send, and who will go for {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}}?" And I said, "Here I [am]; send me."

R.8: Then I heard the voice of the Lord. He asked, "Who can I send? Who will go for {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}}?" I answered, "I am ready! Send me!"

decisions.choice: for us: God speaking with the heavenly court around his throne
alternatives: God speaking of himself in the plural
decisions.reason: The Lord says "I" and then "us". He is surrounded by the seraphim, and in 1 Kings 22:19-22 the prophet Micaiah sees God consulting the heavenly host about whom to send. God also says "us" in Genesis 1:26, 3:22 and 11:7. Christian readers have also heard in the plural a hint of the Trinity.

decisions.choice: here I am: I am ready, at your service
decisions.reason: This is the answer of a servant ready to obey, as with Abraham (Genesis 22:1, 11), Moses (Exodus 3:4) and Samuel (1 Samuel 3:4-8). Isaiah, newly cleansed, offers himself before he knows the message.

decisions.choice: the Lord: the title, as in verse 1
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, the word is the title Adonai, "Lord".

decisions.choice: I am ready
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is "here I [am]", the answer of one ready to serve (see m2). Balanced and Readable say what the expression means. Literal keeps "Here I am".

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֵ֥ךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמ֨וֹעַ֙ וְאַל־תָּבִ֔ינוּ וּרְא֥וּ רָא֖וֹ וְאַל־תֵּדָֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: And he said, go, and you will say to the people this, hear hearing, and do not understand; and see seeing, and do not know.
pieces: He said, "Go, and say to this people: \q 'Hear and hear again, yet do not understand; \q look and look again, yet do not come to know.'

L.9: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Go, and say to this people, \q 'Hear indeed, but do not understand; \q and see indeed, but do not perceive.'

R.9: He said, "Go and give this message to these people: \q 'Keep on listening, but do not understand. \q Keep on looking, but do not learn anything.'

decisions.choice: hear indeed ... see indeed: keep on hearing, keep on seeing
decisions.reason: Each verb is doubled for emphasis: the people will hear and see again and again, yet without understanding.

decisions.choice: do not understand ... do not perceive: a command that announces what will happen
decisions.reason: The commands are spoken in grief and irony. They do not ask the people to refuse; they announce that Isaiah's preaching will meet hearts already closed (1:3; 29:9-14), and that their refusal will become God's judgment on them. Isaiah's question "How long?" (verse 11) shows the weight of the task.

decisions.choice: quoted in the New Testament: Matthew 13:14-15; Mark 4:12; Luke 8:10; John 12:40; Acts 28:26-27
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes these verses to explain why many did not understand his parables, and Paul quotes them in Rome at the end of Acts. The New Testament quotations mostly follow the Septuagint, which turns the commands into statements: "you will indeed hear, but never understand".

records.source: הַשְׁמֵן֙ לֵב־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְאָזְנָ֥יו הַכְבֵּ֖ד וְעֵינָ֣יו הָשַׁ֑ע פֶּן־יִרְאֶ֨ה בְעֵינָ֜יו וּבְאָזְנָ֣יו יִשְׁמָ֗ע וּלְבָב֥וֹ יָבִ֛ין וָשָׁ֖ב וְרָ֥פָא לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Make fat [the] heart of the people this, and its ears make heavy, and its eyes smear over, lest it see with its eyes, and with its ears hear, and its heart understand, and turn, and [one] heal it.
pieces: Fatten the heart of this people, \q weigh down their ears, and smear their eyes shut, \q so that their eyes do not see, their ears do not hear, and their heart does not understand, and they do not turn and find healing.'"

L.10: Make the heart of this people fat, \q and make its ears heavy, and smear its eyes shut, \q lest it see with its eyes, and hear with its ears, and its heart understand, and it turn back, and [one] heal it.'"

R.10: Make the minds of these people dull. \q Make their ears deaf and their eyes blind. \q Otherwise they might see with their eyes and hear with their ears. Their minds might understand. Then they would turn back and be healed.'"

decisions.choice: make fat the heart, make heavy the ears, smear the eyes: make the people unable to take in God's word
decisions.reason: A fat heart is dull and unfeeling (Psalm 119:70; Deuteronomy 32:15). Heavy ears do not hear, and eyes smeared shut do not see. The heart is the seat of thought and will, not only feeling.

decisions.choice: make fat: the prophet's message will harden those who refuse it
decisions.reason: God tells Isaiah to do what his preaching will bring about. Like Pharaoh, who hardened his own heart before God hardened it (Exodus 8:11; 9:12), the people have already refused to listen (5:24; 30:9-11). The Septuagint turns the command into a statement, "the heart of this people has grown dull", and Matthew 13:15 and Acts 28:27 quote that form. John 12:40 says "he has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart".

decisions.choice: turn and be healed: repent and be restored
decisions.reason: To turn is to turn back to God in repentance (1:27; 55:7). Healing is God's restoring of his people (1:5-6; 19:22; 30:26; 57:18). The Hebrew "and [one] heal it" names no healer.

decisions.choice: their ears, their eyes (Balanced and Readable); its ears, its eyes (Literal)
decisions.reason: Hebrew speaks of "this people" as a single person with one heart, ears and eyes. Balanced and Readable use "their", which suits a people in English.

decisions.choice: dull ... deaf ... blind
decisions.reason: Readable explains the pictures of a fat heart, heavy ears and smeared eyes by what they mean.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֕ר עַד־מָתַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י וַיֹּ֡אמֶר עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר֩ אִם־שָׁא֨וּ עָרִ֜ים מֵאֵ֣ין יוֹשֵׁ֗ב וּבָתִּים֙ מֵאֵ֣ין אָדָ֔ם וְהָאֲדָמָ֖ה תִּשָּׁאֶ֥ה שְׁמָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I said, until when, Lord? And he said, until that if have lain waste cities from without inhabitant, and houses from without a person, and the ground is devastated [into] a desolation,
pieces: Then I asked, "How long, Lord?" \q He answered, "Until towns lie in ruins with no one living in them, and houses have no one in them, \q and the farmland is laid waste and left desolate,

L.11: And I said, "Until when, Lord?" \q And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Until cities lie in ruins without inhabitant, and houses without a person, \q and the ground is devastated [into] a desolation,

R.11: Then I asked, "Lord, how long will this last?" \q He answered, "It will last until the cities are destroyed and no one lives in them. \q It will last until the houses are empty and the fields are ruined and deserted.

decisions.choice: until when?: how long?, the question of lament
decisions.reason: The same cry is heard in the Psalms (Psalm 6:4; 13:2-3; 90:13). Isaiah asks how long the people will remain blind and deaf, and how long God's judgment will last.

decisions.choice: cities lie in ruins ... a desolation: the curse of the covenant
decisions.reason: The words echo the warning of Leviticus 26:31-33, where God says the cities of a disobedient people will be ruins and their land a desolation. The ruin came on Judah's towns when Assyria invaded in 701 BC (36:1) and on Jerusalem when Babylon destroyed it in 587/586 BC (2 Kings 25:8-10).

decisions.choice: the ground: the farmed land
decisions.reason: The word means the soil and the fields that feed the people, as distinct from the cities and houses.

decisions.choice: It will last until ...
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long answer into short sentences and repeats "it will last" to keep the link to Isaiah's question.

records.source: וְרִחַ֥ק יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־הָאָדָ֑ם וְרַבָּ֥ה הָעֲזוּבָ֖ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: and sends far away Yahweh the humankind, and great [is] the abandonment in [the] midst of the land.
pieces: and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent the people far off, \q and much of the land lies empty and abandoned.

L.12: and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} removes humankind far away, \q and great [is] the abandonment in the midst of the land.

R.12: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will send the people far away, \q and large parts of the land will be left empty.

decisions.choice: Yahweh sends humankind far away: exile
decisions.reason: God will drive the people out of their land. Assyria took the northern kingdom into exile (2 Kings 17:6), and Babylon took the people of Judah (2 Kings 25:11). God speaks of himself by name, as he often does in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: the abandonment: abandoned places, the deserted land
decisions.reason: The word means "what is forsaken". The same word becomes a name of Zion that God will one day take away: "no longer will you be called Forsaken" (62:4).

records.source: וְע֥וֹד בָּהּ֙ עֲשִׂ֣רִיָּ֔ה וְשָׁ֖בָה וְהָיְתָ֣ה לְבָעֵ֑ר כָּאֵלָ֣ה וְכָאַלּ֗וֹן אֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּשַׁלֶּ֨כֶת֙ מַצֶּ֣בֶת בָּ֔ם זֶ֥רַע קֹ֖דֶשׁ מַצַּבְתָּֽהּ׃פ
records.gloss: And still in it a tenth, and it will return and be for burning, like the terebinth and like the oak, which in felling a stump in them; seed of holiness [is] its stump.
pieces: Should a tenth still be left in it, that too will go to the fire once more, \q like a terebinth or an oak that is felled and leaves only a stump. \q But its stump is a holy seed."

L.13: And [if there is] still a tenth in it, it will again be for burning, \q like the terebinth and like the oak, which at [their] felling [have] a stump in them; \q a seed of holiness [is] its stump."

R.13: Even if a tenth of the people are still left in the land, they too will be burned again. \q They will be like a terebinth tree or an oak tree that is cut down and only its stump is left. \q But that stump is a holy seed."

decisions.choice: a tenth ... will again be for burning: even the remnant will be purged again
alternatives: it will turn back (repent) and be burned
decisions.reason: "It" most likely refers to the tenth that remains. The verb "return" here means "again". "For burning" may also mean "for grazing" or "for stripping" (the same verb in 3:14 and 5:5), but either way judgment comes even on the remnant.

decisions.choice: terebinth and oak: great trees that sprout from the stump
decisions.reason: The terebinth and the oak were large, long-lived trees. Cut down, they could send up new shoots from the stump (Job 14:7-9). The picture is of a people cut down to almost nothing, but not finished.

decisions.choice: a holy seed is its stump: a holy remnant will remain
decisions.reason: "Seed" means offspring. From the stump of the felled people God will raise a holy remnant (4:3; 10:20-22). In 11:1 a shoot comes from the stump of Jesse, and Ezra 9:2 calls the returned exiles "the holy seed".

decisions.choice: at the felling ... in them: the Masoretic text
decisions.reason: The wording of the middle of the verse is difficult. The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) reads differently at "in them", in a form often read as "[the stump] of a high place". The Septuagint lacks the last clause, "a holy seed is its stump". The Masoretic text is followed here. Reviewers should check these readings against the scroll and the Septuagint.

decisions.choice: a tenth of the people ... in the land
decisions.reason: Readable names what "it" and "a tenth" refer to: the land and the people left in it.
